# Vattakkhandhaka (Kd 18)

**ID:** Kd 18
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Vattakkhandhaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m3.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vattakkhandhaka* (Kd 18) is the eighth chapter of the *Cullavagga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka, focusing on proper monastic conduct and etiquette (*vatta*, etymologically connected to Sanskrit *vṛtta* or *vrata*) [Collins; Norman 1983; Entrance to the Vinaya 1969]. It details the behavioral duties and reciprocal observances governing monks in various communal and daily scenarios, including relations between preceptor and pupil, protocols for incoming, resident, and departing monks, and decorum during alms rounds, forest dwelling, and within dining halls, living quarters, restrooms, and saunas. Unlike many other Khandhaka chapters that organize ecclesiastical legal procedures, the *Vattakkhandhaka* contains no formal ecclesiastical acts (*karmavācanā*); rather, its regulations pertain primarily to *abhisamācāra* (minor rules of proper behavior and deportment), displaying close thematic connections with the *sekhiya* training rules [Sung 1999; Entrance to the Vinaya 1969].

 In the Mūlasarvāstivādin tradition, much of this material is incorporated within the *Kṣudrakavastu* [Clarke]. Computational text analysis by DharmaNexus corroborates extensive intra-Pali text reuse between the *Vattakkhandhaka* and the *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), other Khandhakas (such as Kd 15, Kd 14, Kd 11, and Kd 16), and later Vinaya handbooks and sub-commentaries including the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* and *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns several passages with the Tibetan *Vinayasūtra* literature and *Vinayakṣudraka-vastu*, as well as Sanskrit Vinaya fragments [DharmaNexus]. English translation includes that of Bhikkhu Brahmali.
